children: Production growth of nine key infrastructure sectors slowed to a three-month low of 4.8 per cent in August, according to the latest government data released on Monday.
Growth rate was 5 per cent in July and 6.2 per cent in August last year.  During April-August, the pace of growth was higher at 4.3 per cent compared to 2.4 per cent in the same period of 2025-26.

Devendra Kumar Pant, Chief Economist with India Ratings & Research, said that six out of nine sectors that account for approximately 44 per cent of the index recorded slowdown in pushing the overall performance downwards supply-side issues such as energy resource availability and their high prices continued to exert downward pressure – fertilizer production continued to be battered by gas shortage.

Nonetheless, the growth during June-August remained relatively stable at 5.3 per cent, second highest rolling three months growth in new base and higher than average growth in FY25 (4.3 per cent) and FY26 (3 per cent). However, the key is the resolution to West Asia crisis, which appears to be distant as off now. “Ind-Ra expects core sector to grow around 5 per cent in September and October 2026,” Pant said.

According to Madan Sabnavis, Chief Economist with Bank of Baroda, core sector growth has been coming down mainly due to energy sector of coal, crude, gas. Higher growth in refinery products due to exports and domestic consumption. Fertilizer production down as sowing season slows down and imports increase. “We may expect IIP growth of 6-6.5 per cent,” he said.

Rahul Agrawal, Principal Economist at ICRA Ltd Fertiliser, said that fertilizer output contracted for the sixth consecutive month in August, following the onset of the West Asia crisis, with the pace of the same widening to double digits in the month. Among the construction-related sectors, while steel output growth inched up slightly in August, it remained lacklustre at just 3.4 per cent. However, cement output expanded by double digits for the second straight month in August 2026.

Besides, electricity generation surged by 11.6 per cent in August, amid healthy growth in demand, supporting the overall growth in core output in the month. Excluding this, “core output rose by just 1.6 per cent in the month (vs. +3.4 per cent in July 2026). Given these trends, “we expect the IIP growth to ease to 5-6 per cent in August 2026 from 6.7 per cent in July 2026,” Agrawal said.

title: Core sector growth down to 4.8% in August
